Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Replayable party lobbies

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Local name preferences

Use Lobby(N) for replayable readiness, leader and run-start rules. It is a value inside the game's World. It contains bounded display names, present/ready masks, a party leader, Waiting/Playing phase and a run counter. Transport ownership and credentials stay in Session/Room. A party leader is a game permission; becoming a network authority does not itself execute Start.

Odin
import lb "godot:replay/lobby"

party := lb.initial(4) // waiting; leader seat 1
lb.roster(&party, joins, leaves) // recorded simulation roster changes
name, ok := lb.name("Torch keeper")
result := lb.apply(&party, seat, {verb=.Ready, name=name, ready=true})
result = lb.apply(&party, seat, {verb=.Start})
if result == .Started {
    // Initialize this game's encounter and clocks at the current simulation tick.
}

Commands are ordinary game actions, validated by the game's model and admitted through the existing network runner. Ready can set a name and readiness atomically. A separate Profile command clears readiness only when its name actually changes; repeating the same profile is a no-op on readiness. Names are trimmed, clipped to 48 UTF-8 bytes without splitting a rune, and reject empty/control/line-separator values. Stored names require canonical zero tails. Names are cosmetic, not accounts or authorization identities; games can impose additional naming policy.

Only a present party leader can Start, and every present player must be ready. A recorded departure removes readiness. A newly present/reconnected seat must ready again. If a leader departs, the lowest present seat becomes leader. There is no out-of-band election of game permissions. reset_member clears a freshly assigned seat's profile/readiness; it should accompany the game's existing fresh player reset callback, not every reconnect.

initial(N, automatic=true) uses leader zero and lets auto_start transition once all present players are ready. This suits dedicated-server staging. Automatic restart is an application policy. Restart requires the party leader and explicit can_restart=true from the game's completed-run condition. It increments the run counter and leaves names/roster intact; the game decides which inventory, entities, clocks and cumulative statistics to reset. Check Result before applying those consequences. Observers do not occupy these player seats.

valid checks bounds and name representations. The caller supplies valid roster masks/seat counts and integrates the lobby with its own gameplay predicates. The component allocates no heap storage in roster/command processing. Its name helpers use borrowed views over fixed value storage; do not retain text(&name) after that value moves or dies.

Local name preferences#

profile_encode / profile_decode provide a bounded version-1 preference format. It stores a display name, not a credential or gameplay checkpoint. Godot's Name_Profile adapter reads/writes that preference outside simulation:

Odin
storagegd.name_profile_open(&profile, "user://display_name", "my-game", true, initial_name)
// Poll even while a session is connecting or while the main menu is showing.
storagegd.name_profile_frame(&profile)
storagegd.name_profile_set(&profile, edited_name)
// At owner teardown:
storagegd.name_profile_close(&profile)

Native storage uses a flushed staging file and rename, with one writer per path. Browser storage uses the existing IndexedDB service and revision-checked writes. Reading/writing is observable through phase and dirty; malformed data and CAS conflicts set failed and preserve existing storage. An application may still use an explicitly entered name for the current session while reporting that preference failure. Wait for pending writes when persistence matters before teardown.

The native Cavecrawl gate drives real buttons and reloads the name in a fresh process, including corrupt-file preservation. The browser gate closes and launches a new Chrome process with the same isolated profile, removes the URL name override, and reads the persisted name through the actual menu.
